To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elderly patients using multiple medications have many drug-related problems (DRPs), and the more drugs patients use, the higher the risk of DRPs.
the number of DRP is related to the number and the type of prescribed drugs and that community pharmacists can play a role in resolving and preventing DRP.

drug-related problems are frequent following hospital discharge among elderly patients using 5 or more drugs for chronic diseases and that the number of drug-related problems increases with the number of prescribed drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of tools and methods to identify and resolve drug-related problems in elderly patients discharged from hospitals.
the identification and resolution of DRP in elderly patients using community pharmacists as the first line of defence.
the identification of DRPs in elderly patients discharged from the hospital and the development and evaluation of interventions for the prevention of DRPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the number of DRP in elderly people using multiple drugs is related to the number drugs used and that a specific identification tool developed for use by the community pharmacist is an appropriate method for identifying DRP.
the occurrence of DRPs in elderly patients is high and that the community pharmacists are in a position to identify and resolve DRPs.
elderly people who are prescribed five or more medications have an increased risk of experiencing drug related problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the number of drug-related problems increased with the number and complexity of the drugs prescribed and that a significant proportion of these problems were related to the lack of patient knowledge about drug use.
we have developed an identification tool for the detection of drug-related problems in elderly patients using multiple medicines following hospital discharge.
we have developed a tool to identify and resolve drug-related problems among elderly patients using a minimum of five drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
community pharmacists can play a key role in the identification and prevention of DRP.
community pharmacists can play a key role in the identification, prevention, and resolution of DRP in elderly patients discharged from hospitals.
DRP are common among elderly hospital patients and are related to the number and complexity of the drugs prescribed.
